title: Quick Sort
problemStatement: Sort an array using Quick Sort (Lomuto or Hoare partition).
intuition: Partition around a pivot: left ≤ pivot ≤ right (policy depends on scheme), then recurse. Average O(n log n), worst O(n²) on bad pivots (sorted array + poor pivot) → TLE risk; randomize or use median-of-three. In-place: O(log n) stack average.

approaches.title: Quick sort (Lomuto partition)
approaches.idea: Pivot = last element; grow ≤ region with i; recurse.
approaches.time: Average O(n log n); worst O(n²)
approaches.space: O(log n) avg stack; O(n) worst stack
limitations: Sorted input + last-element pivot → worst O(n²) TLE; randomize pivot in interviews
approaches.whyWorks: After partition, pivot is in final sorted index; recurse on independent sides.

specialTechnique.title: Avoiding worst-case TLE
specialTechnique.body: Random pivot or median-of-three. For guaranteed O(n log n), use mergesort / heapsort / library sort (introsort). Mention 3-way partition for many duplicates.

complexity.time: Avg O(n log n); worst O(n²)

patternRecognition: Quickselect uses same partition for k-th element
interviewInsight: Must discuss average vs worst case and pivot strategy — otherwise you look shallow.
